messages.text:
"Create a fast-paced 2D vector-art arcade city defense game inspired by 'Utopia Must Fall'.

### VISUAL @COMMENT_BODY@ AUDIO STYLE
- Retro vector graphics with bright neon lines (cyan, magenta, yellow, white) against a stark black sky.
- Minimalism with high contrast. Crisp pixel explosions, particle trails, and screen-shake on impact.
- Synthwave/chiptune vibe with punchy sound effects for firing, explosions, and target locking.

### SCENE SETUP @COMMENT_BODY@ PERSPECTIVE
- Fixed 2D side-view camera showing a single screen.
- ENVIRONMENT:
  * Bottom of screen: A flat ground plane containing a detailed futuristic city skyline (buildings, neon signs, glowing windows).
  * Middle of screen: A raised defense platform equipped with 2 primary turrets (Left and Right).
  * Top of screen: Dark night sky/space where incoming enemy waves spawn and descend.

### PLAYER CONTROLS @COMMENT_BODY@ WEAPONS
- CONTROL SCHEME: Aim with mouse crosshair. 
  * Left Click: Fire Main Laser (fast trajectory, precise point-defense).
  * Right Click: Fire Heavy Missile (slower, splash/AoE explosion to clear clusters).
  * Spacebar: Trigger Emergency EMP (cooldown-based screen-wipe, limited uses per round).
- AMMO SYSTEM: Main weapon uses heat/overheat management (cannot hold down fire indefinitely). Missiles have limited ammo per wave.

### ENEMIES @COMMENT_BODY@ WAVE SPAWNING
- Enemies spawn from the top edge and rain down toward the city:
  1. Missiles/Rockets: Fast, straight trajectories targeting specific buildings.
  2. Cluster Bombs: Split into 3 smaller warheads midway down.
  3. Shielded Drones: Hover horizontally, shooting smaller projectiles before diving.
  4. Heavy Boss Ships: High health, spawn every 5 waves, rain down dense missile barrages.

### CORE GAMEPLAY LOOP @COMMENT_BODY@ UPGRADES
- OBJECTIVE: Protect the city buildings from destruction across progressively harder waves.
- CITY HEALTH: Each building has individual health. If all buildings are destroyed, GAME OVER.
- BETWEEN-WAVE SHOP / UPGRADES:
  * Earning credits per enemy destroyed and surviving city percentage.
  * Spend credits between waves on:
    - Defense Repairs (Restore building integrity)
    - Turret Fire Rate @COMMENT_BODY@ Overheat Limit
    - Missile Blast Radius @COMMENT_BODY@ Ammo Capacity
    - Auto-Interceptors (Autonomous point-defense drones)
    - EMP Cooldown Reduction

### UI @COMMENT_BODY@ HUD
- Top bar: Current Wave, Score, Credits, and EMP Cooldown indicator.
- Bottom bar: Health bars for individual city buildings.
- Overheat gauge attached to the mouse cursor for quick feedback. (2D Game, Phone/Tablet)

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

## Repository findings

- **No existing app or game entry point is present.** The repository has no root `index.html`, `src/`, `public/`, app JavaScript/TypeScript, or `package.json`.
- **No project game assets are present.** There are no root-level images, audio, models, or other game content to build on.
- The tracked project content is essentially the README and an OpenCode GitHub Actions workflow:
  - `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/README.md` — project links and OMGithub boilerplate.
  - `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/.github/workflows/opencode.yml` — automation workflow, not app tooling.
- Startup/capture scripts delegate to scripts supplied through an external runtime:
  - `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/start.sh` runs `${RUNTIME_DIR}/scripts/default-start.mjs`.
  - `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/capture.sh` runs `${RUNTIME_DIR}/scripts/default-capture.mjs`.
  - `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/startup.sh` only enables strict shell options.
  - There are no repository-defined npm scripts or app-specific build/test commands.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/Agents.md` includes browser-capture and mobile-game guidance, including responsive layouts and touch controls. It is guidance, not an existing implementation.

## Recommendation

Implement the game as a small, self-contained browser app with new root-level files such as:

- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html` — browser entry point and UI structure.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js` — gameplay, rendering, and input.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/styles.css` — presentation and responsive layout.
- Add an `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/assets/` directory only if the game needs external assets.

There is a Three.js GLB-viewer example under `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/.agents/skills/load-sketchfab-threejs/assets/viewer/`, with its own `index.html`, `main.js`, and `styles.css`. It is a skill resource rather than project code, and there are no game-ready model assets there; treat it as an optional reference only, not the app entry point.

Built a complete, playable neon city-defense game in `index.html`, `styles.css`, and `game.js`.

It includes mouse and touch controls, laser heat management, limited heavy missiles, a once-per-wave EMP, four enemy types and boss waves every fifth wave, destructible city buildings, credits and between-wave upgrades, and synthesized arcade sound effects. Waves continue with increasing difficulty.

To play, serve the project directory locally and open `index.html`. I verified the JavaScript syntax and that the page is served successfully. I couldn’t capture a browser screenshot because Chromium isn’t installed in this environment.

Assumptions: each wave grants one EMP use; shops appear after a wave is cleared; control hints adapt for mobile.
